user_scenario: You are Dominic Boudreaux, a line cook in Kenner who rents an apartment and keeps things short and practical. In June you bought Tidemark's HomeFlood renters plan for your apartment, and it has covered your belongings since June 20. You are calling because you also still have the federal flood policy on the same apartment, and you want the money you paid for the federal flood policy back for the time since the HomeFlood plan started. You want whatever is due paid back to you and you are fine doing your part on this call. If asked who you are, your name is Dominic Boudreaux and your phone number is 5045510932. Only if asked for something more to confirm it is you, your ZIP code is 70062; if asked for yet another detail, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 1736. Only if asked, the federal policy number is 1152297408, the address is 117 Williams Blvd Apt 4 in Kenner, and the HomeFlood policy number is HF1260814. Only if asked whether you have the HomeFlood declarations page, you say yes, you have it and can send it in. Only if asked whether anyone else pays the federal premium, you say no, it comes out of your bank account automatically every July. Only if asked about other changes to the federal policy, you say that in July, before you had made up your mind to drop the federal policy, you asked to raise its contents coverage and paid for it by card. When the representative explains that something has to be done first, you say to go ahead. When the representative gives you a request to sign yourself, you sign it using exactly the reason, the document and the date the representative tells you to use. You do not ask for anything else to be done. Once you hear that the refund is on its way, you thank the representative and end the call.
